screen: Production Business Search (desktop 1440, full page), Stage 5 pass 3

expected_differences: Search correctly has a query field, clear control, Search action and a muted result count rather than Home’s attention links, city selector and discovery tabs.
Demo Coffee Co., the six returned people, their locations, supplied images and D/L initial fallbacks replace the Lab fixtures. Do not manufacture portraits or remove source-backed demo titles.
The complete, multirow result gallery is appropriate for Search. Actual source ratios explain why these spreads do not reproduce the Lab’s three-person opening ribbon.
Business remains current in the rail while Search is selected as the utility destination, as requested.
The Request dropdown is a valid entry to the existing request choices; it does not need to reproduce the Lab’s personalized button labels.
A query result need not include Home’s default vehicle inventory. No Cars section is visible here, but that alone does not establish a broken car search or justify adding fixture vehicles.
The price embedded in Priya’s supplied creative is source content, not TapMart compensation. No unsolicited people price has been added.
keep: The mineral #F4F3EF canvas, #101820 rail, restrained reversed lockup and flat, shadow-free working field.
The 200px rail, main origin at x=232, 32px desktop gutter and approximately 36/40px page title.
Open source-ratio spreads with 4px media corners, 32px/52px identity offsets and no oversized landscape letterboxes.
The 18/24px person names, supporting 14/20px city and provenance text, and muted People count.
Visible View person and Request actions, the cobalt Search decision and the prominent keyboard-focus treatment.
Literal, separate Instagram and creator-verification states; these should remain tied to their stored records.
review.readiness_note: Visible business context, query entry, clearing, search submission, person navigation and request entry remain exposed. A capture cannot verify their execution or car-query coverage. Before release, exercise a car-matching query, independent empty/error states and the named-recipient request handoff. Visual sign-off remains blocked by the caption issues below.

drift.change: Stop shrinking the source link into an unreadable fragment. Give the actual work title a full-width IBM Plex Sans 14/20px line with white-space: normal, overflow: visible and overflow-wrap: anywhere. Put the existing provenance on the following 14/20px line when necessary. Preserve the real title and inspection destination; do not substitute invented fit labels.
drift.why: Jasmine’s source title is reduced to '[demo] Recr…', while demo-creator and Marcus show little beyond '[demo]…'. The metadata survives at the expense of the work being requested. This is especially unhelpful beside the uniform red reference, whose clipped title provides almost no identification.
drift.where: People captions, particularly Jasmine Reed, demo-creator and Marcus Bell.

drift.change: Remove follower totals, completed counts, rating scores and review counts from Search’s root people captions. Retain them in person detail. Keep the root hierarchy at name/city 18/24px and 14/20px, readable source title plus literal provenance 14/20px, then View person and Request with minimum 44px targets. Use the freed caption space to resolve source-title truncation.
drift.why: Production restores lines such as '12.4K followers · 2 completed · 5.0 rating · 2 reviews' and '3.2K followers'. The approved shared discovery treatment explicitly moves reputation into detail so the work and request—not popularity—organize the encounter.
drift.where: Reputation rows beneath the people’s source/provenance captions.

review.why: The shell, typography, neutral surfaces, source ratios and open identity/work relationships closely follow Frame Shift. Production also retains visible business-search controls without introducing fake portraits, vehicle models, earnings or decorative cards. The material regression is in the captions: reputation summaries have returned, while actual work titles are compressed into nearly meaningless fragments. That reverses the approved source-first hierarchy. The missing default car shelf is not itself drift on a filtered Search screen, and vehicle money or offer behavior cannot be assessed from this capture.
review.verdict: Frame Shift is largely present and visible search functionality survives, but the reputation-heavy, truncated people captions prevent a faithful-transfer sign-off.
